Arrays and data science

NumPy and pandas make Python the default for numeric and data work. Guion now has native arrays and a first-party data-frame library, frames, but both are young. In the project's reports on one Apple M1 Pro, frames finishes five tested CSV workloads before pandas does from start to finish, mostly because pandas takes about 0.27 s to load. On compute alone, against pandas 3.1.1 and NumPy 2.5.4 and with a development build of 0.9.1, Guion is ahead on four tests: reading a 1,000,000-row CSV takes 0.77 times what pandas takes (for repeated reads in one process; the first read in a process measured 0.93), element-wise maths 0.77 times what NumPy takes, summing 0.83 times, and sorting a million numbers 0.68 times. Matrix multiplication takes 1.96 times what NumPy takes: Guion uses only documented processor instructions, while NumPy's library on Apple M1 to M3 uses an undocumented matrix unit.

Earlier tests that reached NumPy through Python are retired and no longer cited. These figures are from the 25 November speed report, one run of each test on one machine, on a development build of 0.9.1 (evaluation/completion/results/2026-11-25-speed-report.md in the repository).
